title: Sunday cron uses --volumes on docker prune
description: The crontab entry `0 5 * * 0 docker system prune -a -f --volumes` includes the --volumes flag, which deletes ALL unused Docker volumes. If any service container is stopped during the 04:30 auto-rebuild window, its data volume could be deleted.
remediation: SSH to Pi: `crontab -e` → remove --volumes so the entry reads: `0 5 * * 0 docker system prune -a -f`

title: Backblaze B2 storage cap hit
description: The B2 backup upload failed with HTTP 403 on 2026-01-15. No successful offsite backup has been confirmed since then. The current DR posture for INFRA and APPS cannot be trusted until capacity is verified.
remediation: Check the Backblaze B2 console for bucket usage. Delete old backup versions or upgrade the storage cap. Re-run backup manually: `sudo /home/adrianzinko/scripts/backup.sh`

title: Nextcloud file data (26 GB) has no offsite backup
description: `INCLUDE_NEXTCLOUD_DATA_TO_B2=0` in backup.sh excludes photos and videos from B2 uploads. The 26 GB of Nextcloud files (photos, videos) are only on the local NVMe — a disk failure means permanent loss.
remediation: Set `INCLUDE_NEXTCLOUD_DATA_TO_B2=1` in backup.sh and verify B2 storage cap has enough headroom first. Alternatively, add a separate rclone sync job targeting a cold storage bucket.

title: Cert renewal runs bi-monthly — narrow buffer
description: Certs expire in 90 days. The renewal cron runs on the 1st of every other month (bi-monthly). One missed run leaves only ~30 days of buffer before expiry, which is too tight for a manually-intervened recovery.
remediation: Change the cron from bi-monthly (`0 4 1 */2 *`) to monthly (`0 4 1 * *`): `crontab -e` on the Pi.
